overview: White plays 3.e4 against the Slav, a Diemer-Duhm style gambit: 3...dxe4 4.Nc3 and White develops quickly with f3, Bg5, Bc4 or Nxe4 for the pawn. Black has a solid pawn on c6 and the extra pawn, and can usually return it to get a good position. White looks for a kingside attack.

white_ideas.idea: Develop with Nc3, f3 or Bg5 for a pawn, using the open e-file and lines to attack
Play Bc4 and Nxe4 hitting f7 and the kingside
Recapture on e4 with a knight and keep a lead in development

black_ideas.idea: Take on e4, play ...e5 or ...Nf6 and return the pawn at the right moment
Develop the c8 bishop first with ...Bf5 or ...Bg4
Keep the extra pawn and trade queens

typical_structures.structure: Black extra pawn on e4, or the pawn returned and an open centre
Open e- and d-files with Black's c6/d5 structure broken

character.notes: A gambit with quick development against a king that has not castled; forcing and tactical if Black grabs and plays on.

gambit.notes: 3...dxe4 wins a pawn that Black can often keep for a time but gives back to get a safe position.

soundness.notes: Strong players think the Diemer gambits against the Slav do not give enough for the pawn.

approach.notes: Played for surprise, seldom chosen by strong players; offbeat.

sublines_that_differ.name: 3...e6
sublines_that_differ.how: Black ignores the gambit and heads for a French-style structure with ...dxe4 later.

character.reason: A White gambit with open lines and quick attacking ideas.

gambit.reason: White offers the e4 pawn for development.

soundness.reason: Considered not enough for the pawn.

approach.reason: Seldom chosen against the Slav by strong players.

level.reason: A dubious gambit is never Beginner.

plans.reason: White gives a pawn for development and attack.
